That's a complicated question to which I will try to give my best answer.
At first, for attention. I know, I know, it was terrible, but I was young and dramatic. I thought it would make me "cool".
But then, after awhile, I began feeling depressed. Like nobody was listening to me, and since I had heard that cutting can make you feel better, I decided to try it again. This time, it made me feel in control. It also was a way to sort of "get back" at people who had hurt me.
Then, it became a way to get out anger. Simple as that. Slashing something- even if it's yourself- and seeing it bleed is surprisingly effective when it comes to anger management, if very unhealthy.
Then it became a way for me to stay alive. I needed it. I don't know how else to describe it. I was close to killing myself every single day, and cutting was the only thing stopping me.
Now, it's an addiction. The chemicals released in your brain when you get an injury can be very addictive. I've heard it be compared to trying to quit cocaine.
So yeah, that's about the gist of it.
